analyst_view.overall: Juventus are 5th with 10 points and unbeaten in Europe, and a win would put them close to a top-eight place; Omonia (18th, 6 points) are in the play-off places but lost their last two European games. Luciano Spalletti goes to Como on Sunday and the Italian press expects heavy rotation: Conceicao, Sarr, Boga, McKennie and Gatti are tipped to start, with Woltemade or Kolo Muani up front. Yildiz, Locatelli, Thuram and Grabara are out and one report says Zhegrova is unavailable; the numbers only take something off for Locatelli. Kerim Alajbegovic trained with the group again on Wednesday, so he may be on the bench. Omonia under Henning Berg are without Carel Eiting, have Loic Nego back and Lois Diony has scored in three straight games; English referee Samuel Barrott (about 4.0 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Juventus 2.0) and take only a little off for Locatelli. They do not see Yildiz's absence or a heavily changed side before Como, so I go lower; Alajbegovic being back in training and Diony's form for Omonia make the cut a bit smaller than this morning, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, mostly Juventus (8.0), already up for their 44 corners in the last six games. Omonia will defend deep, which the split already shows, but a reshuffled Juventus without Yildiz should pin them back a little less, so I shade it to about 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already trimmed because Juventus have drawn few bookings lately (5 in six) and Omonia have been calm, with referee Samuel Barrott close to average (4.0 a game). A one-sided game with Omonia defending tends to stay quiet and rotation does not change that, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, with Omonia's recent shooting already adding about 15% to their side. A Juventus side with several changes and no Yildiz should create a bit less, though Spalletti wants a quicker build-up than in the first half against Venezia, so I go to about 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, 7.6 of them for Juventus. With Yildiz out and the attack rebuilt around Conceicao, Boga, McKennie and Woltemade or Kolo Muani, Juventus's finishing should be a little less sharp, so I go to about 9.7.
